title: Verify that the generated app actually works
summary: Project checks distinguish unit tests from real integration and application journeys. Frozen checks run against fresh workspaces, inspect real outputs and preserve concrete runtime blockers. Failed checks feed repairs without weakening their expectations. Resumed and self-healing runs create their verification artifacts even when baseline tests are cached.
benefit: Passing tests with fake backends can no longer establish product readiness. Missing models, empty processing results and broken playback remain visible.
where: Projects milestone evidence; run verification artifacts; swarmforge verify

title: Keep moving when later features are already built
summary: Milestones can evaluate earlier merged project work without requiring a redundant build. Unavailable browser observations remain on the final review list. Large Pi instructions travel as file references through both host and container process launches.
benefit: Avoid repeated evidence-only tasks and command-length failures while preserving passing-test requirements and the approved spending cap.
where: Projects > milestone evaluation and recovery

title: Know when the project needs you
summary: Automatic planning and task activity are labelled No input needed, with a direct link to the active task. Paused or stopped workers offer Run approved work on the project. Refresh status checks current progress, and an open dashboard offers a reload when newer controls are available.
benefit: Avoid mistaking the lead choosing work for a question, and get an actionable control when the worker has stopped.
where: Projects > open a running project > Project progress

title: Let the swarm recover and build a preview while you are away
summary: Optional unattended delivery repairs routine planning and ordering problems, retries safe interruptions and temporary environment failures, and reallocates remaining approved project funds to bounded task recovery. Missing milestone evidence gets an automatic verification pass; unavailable observations remain pending while later software milestones continue. The final preview review gathers all unverified checks. Resolved planning errors are clearly labelled as history.
benefit: Return to a reviewable preview with fewer internal problems handed back to you, while retaining spending history, verification results and the approved project cap.
where: Projects → approved project; projects.autonomous in configuration

title: Understand project stops and approve recovery in one click
summary: Project decisions name the stopped task, show passed and unresolved checks, and explain each choice. Verify and fix automatically keeps a milestone open; explicit acceptance confirms listed checks. Exhausted tasks offer a specific additional allowance and time window while retaining spending and evidence. Removed pending plans no longer count as failed builds. Launch and recovery controls use clear approval buttons without redundant checkboxes. Fully verified milestones can advance automatically when the approved spec requests no further approval.
benefit: See exactly why work paused and what continuing authorizes, without approving an unexplained stop or retrying an exhausted task unchanged.
where: Projects → open a stopped project → Project decision

title: Recover automatically from planning errors and understand a pause
summary: The lead repairs invalid responses with exact validation feedback and valid examples within its persisted decision allowance. It can continue an existing accepted task without recreating it or discarding later work. Rejected proposals have readable explanations and expandable details. A planning stop offers Retry planning automatically with optional clarification; approved scope can be revised in a guarded editor when needed. Real milestone checks, uncertain actions, merges and spending limits keep their existing protections.
benefit: Internal response-format errors no longer leave you guessing or repairing the planner's JSON. Keep the project moving and make a concrete decision only when one is needed.
where: Projects → open a paused project → Planning and recovery; Edit approved scope

title: Follow each task through a clear, tabbed workspace
summary: Expand a task on Work to see its current stage, finished bot assignments, acceptance checks and spend at a glance. Separate tabs show the dependency sequence and repair cycles, the bots and models actually recorded, checks, retained files, searchable activity and controls. Long results open only when you need them, pending approvals stay visible, and the selected tab is remembered for each task.
benefit: Understand what the swarm has done, what it is working on and what needs your attention without scrolling through a wall of logs.
where: Work or History → expand a task → Overview, Sequence, Bots, Checks, Files, Activity or Controls

title: Watch replies arrive, copy code and download files in chat
summary: General and project conversations share a new message layout: your messages appear on the right and assistant replies on the left. Code blocks have copy and download buttons, replies can be copied or saved as Markdown, tables and images render inline, and generated files appear as download cards. Replies stream from the model as they arrive and reconnect when needed. Interrupted text and any completed files stay in the conversation.
benefit: Read long answers while they are being written, use code without selecting it by hand, and keep files and images beside the discussion that produced them.
where: Chat; Projects → Conversation; try python scripts/react_dashboard.py --demo for a simulated streaming reply with code, CSV and an image

title: Turn a short kickoff into a proposal, with questions you can fill in
summary: Describe your project in a short form. The lead can ask one round of product questions as fields or choices, then drafts the specification and milestones for review. Optional details get editable defaults, including a proposed allowance and a new repository under your configured GitHub account. Missing model fields are filled in without asking you to type None or debug a spec. A malformed draft gets one repair attempt, then a labelled starter proposal if needed.
benefit: Get to a concrete project proposal without an endless interview about setup details. Scope, repository and spending still need your approval before launch.
where: Projects → New project → Draft my project; configure projects.default_repo_owner and projects.default_budget_usd

title: Review and launch tasks suggested in chat
summary: Chat keeps generated task suggestions with the reply and shows a review button for each one. Edit the repository, requirements and allowance, then authorize Launch task to queue it and start the worker. A suggestion stays linked to its queued task across reloads and cannot queue twice.
benefit: Turn a conversation into work without copying the task into another page or losing the model's suggestions.
where: Chat → assistant task suggestions → Review and launch task

title: Plan a new project in chat, then launch its reviewed proposal
summary: New project opens a kickoff conversation instead of a blank requirements form. When the proposal is ready, review its specification, milestones and budget before Approve and launch. Approval and checkpoint continuation start the worker; a startup problem leaves the approved work saved and explains how to start it from Work.
benefit: Discuss the idea before filling in details, and have an approved project begin without a separate queue-start step.
where: Projects → New project; Chat → Start a project

title: Interrupted pushes, PRs and merges are checked on GitHub instead of blocking retries
summary: If SwarmForge stopped in the middle of pushing a branch, opening a draft PR, merging or closing a PR, it now asks GitHub what actually happened: done (it continues from the real result), not done (safe to do once more), or a conflict that needs you. It happens automatically when the worker or web interface starts and before a task is retried; `swarmforge reconcile` does it on demand. The evidence for every verdict is kept.
benefit: A crash at the wrong moment no longer leaves a task stuck with “needs reconciliation”, and nothing is pushed or merged twice.
where: CLI: swarmforge reconcile (also automatic)

title: Background work has one owner and recovers cleanly
summary: Chat replies and project-lead turns are now durable jobs with a single owner and a renewable lease. A second web window or a restart never interrupts work another live process owns; work whose process died is marked interrupted (or uncertain, for the project lead) with the reason recorded, and is never replayed automatically. Your chat message is saved before the reply starts, so a crash never loses it.
benefit: No more stuck replies or lost messages after a restart, and no duplicate project-lead actions.
where: Chat, Projects (automatic)

title: Rename chats, and new chats name themselves
summary: Click the pencil next to a conversation's name to rename it (Enter saves, Escape cancels). After the first reply, an unnamed chat gets a short title written by the chat model, or taken from your first message if that call fails. A name you chose is never replaced.
benefit: No more lists full of identical "New chat" entries; you can find a conversation again at a glance.
where: Chat → conversation header

title: Long conversations and agent sessions are summarized instead of forgotten
summary: When a chat or project-lead conversation outgrows its context window, the older messages are summarized (incrementally, once) and the summary is sent with the recent messages. Agents whose transcript grows very long summarize their earlier tool turns while keeping the latest ones intact. Summary calls are charged to the same allowance.
benefit: Long chats keep earlier decisions in view, and long agent sessions stop running out of context.
where: Chat, project kickoff conversations and agent runs (automatic)

title: A calmer project page with a clear status and next step
summary: A project now opens on a short summary (status in plain words, what went wrong with a suggested fix, milestone, tasks and spending) plus any decision waiting for you. Milestones, tasks, the lead conversation and the spec/history live in tabs. Drafts open on the conversation tab.
benefit: You see what matters (is it moving, is it stuck, what to do) without scrolling through every milestone and event.
where: Projects → open a project

title: Just press Send
summary: Chat and project conversations no longer ask you to tick a box before each message. Press Send or Enter (Shift+Enter for a new line). A reply that is still running in another browser or a second web window keeps running instead of being marked interrupted.
benefit: Conversations feel like chat again, and a second window never cuts off a reply. Launching projects, starting the queue and retries still ask first.
where: React dashboard → Chat, Projects

title: Retries fold by task, not by title
summary: Work groups the attempts of one task using its recorded retry history, so two different tasks that happen to share a title stay separate, and a renamed retry still joins its task.
benefit: The attempt count you see is the real number of tries for that task.
where: React dashboard → Work

title: An old tab cannot act on a different workspace
summary: If the web interface is restarted with another workspace (for example the demo replaced by your real one), an open tab shows an out-of-date banner and its buttons are refused until you reload. Drafts are kept per workspace, and Windows-edited knowledge notes now read correctly.
benefit: No accidental actions from a forgotten tab, and notes from Windows editors show clean titles.
where: React dashboard, all pages

title: Follow chat replies as they happen, with attachments
summary: The React chat shows each reply's progress and the tools it checked, keeps failures visible with the reason, and accepts screenshots and text files with thumbnails.
benefit: You can see a slow reply is still working, recover a failed message in one click, and ask about a screenshot or log without leaving the page.
where: React dashboard → Chat

title: Merge pull requests, read post-mortems and edit notes in the React dashboard
summary: Pull requests can be merged or updated after you confirm your review; merges are refused if new commits arrived since. Failures show why each run failed and what to do next, and knowledge notes, including subfolders, can be created and edited.
benefit: Finish the day's review without switching dashboards, and never merge code you have not seen.
where: React dashboard → Pull requests, Failures, Knowledge

title: Settings, Speed and Benchmarks in the React dashboard
summary: Edit role models, temperatures, steps and limits with the same validation and backup as before, run health checks and model tests, see where run time goes, and compare benchmark suites. Work now folds repeated attempts and can archive finished runs.
benefit: Tune the swarm and judge the effect from one interface, with a clear note when a restart is needed.
where: React dashboard → Settings, Speed, Benchmarks, Work

title: Choose a balanced model team
summary: The balanced team combines a Qwen4 project lead, DeepSeek backend developer, MiMo frontend developer and independent GLM reviewer, with explicit backups and screenshot-capable model settings.
benefit: Try the selected lineup without changing task budgets, permissions or developer harnesses. Its quality and delivery cost still need benchmark verification.
where: Model team → balanced; or team: balanced in configuration

title: Use a dedicated React dashboard for your swarm
summary: The optional React dashboard brings Work, task creation, project planning and checkpoints, conversations, evidence, notes, model teams and history into one workspace. Explicit local controls reuse existing approval and spending rules. An interactive demo uses temporary data and simulated models.
benefit: Follow evidence and take common actions without switching pages in Streamlit. Browser drafts survive navigation, and duplicate requests cannot silently repeat completed work.
where: From a checkout, run python scripts/react_dashboard.py --demo; use --allow-actions for configured workspace controls. See docs/WEB_INTERFACE.md.

title: See why the project lead chose its next action
summary: The lead can inspect evidence, queue bounded investigations or reviewed tasks, update the unfinished plan, evaluate a milestone or ask a concrete question. Application code validates each action and records whether it applied, failed, was rejected or needs you.
benefit: You can inspect the evidence behind decisions, while persisted action and spending limits prevent repeated inspections or endless replanning. Browser journey requests are explicitly unverified until a runner is available.
where: Projects → Plan decision events; swarmforge project status PROJECT_ID → lead_decisions

title: Keep retries within one task allowance
summary: Tasks and their retries share persisted time and spending limits. Repeated actions, recurring failures and inactivity stop work, with bounded recovery and retained evidence. Uncertain publication is held for review.
benefit: Restarting a worker or retrying a task cannot quietly replenish its allowance or repeat a recorded external action.
where: Work → task details → Task allowance and progress; Projects activity; execution reports; swarmforge status

title: Choose and compare model teams
summary: Pick a whole lineup of models by name: the current Chinese team, an American premium team (Anthropic Claude via DeepInfra) or an American open-weight team (NVIDIA Nemotron, OpenAI gpt-oss, Google Gemma). Fallback models always come from the same team.
benefit: Run the same benchmark tasks with several teams and compare delivery rate, time and cost per success side by side, each team within its own budget.
where: New task / queue / Projects → Model team; Benchmarks; `swarmforge teams`, `swarmforge bench-suite --teams ...`

title: Plan improvements to SwarmForge itself
summary: Start an improvement project with the SwarmForge repository selected. Use the kickoff chat to agree on milestones, checks and a budget before launching.
benefit: Plan a larger improvement across several milestones and track the resulting tasks on Work.
where: Projects → Improve SwarmForge

title: Build an app through milestones
summary: Start with a kickoff conversation, review a written spec, then launch a project that plans from the real repository after each merged task. Milestone reports give you checkpoints to review and correct the direction.
benefit: You can guide a whole app without managing a long list of tasks planned on assumptions.
where: Projects → Start a project

title: Keep track of new features
summary: Browse feature highlights by date, search by topic, and see where each feature lives in the app. Mark highlights as read when you have caught up.
benefit: You can understand what changed without reading Git commits or remembering every development task.
where: What's new

title: A cleaner SwarmForge workspace
summary: Your hive artwork now appears in the sidebar and welcome screen. Orange accents, clearer spacing and task summary cards make the Work page easier to scan on desktop and phone.
benefit: Spot running work, upcoming tasks and items needing attention at a glance.
where: Work and Getting started

title: Faster chat actions and quieter tool details
summary: Use slash shortcuts and pasted URLs to get to common chat actions. Tool activity can be expanded when you need the details, and tools can be turned on or off.
benefit: Move through routine questions with less typing and less transcript clutter.
where: Chat

title: Let chat inspect a workspace safely
summary: Optional file reading, search and command tools run against a read-only workspace in an isolated Docker container. Shell commands are disabled by default.
benefit: Investigate code and failures from the conversation while keeping workspace files protected.
where: Chat; enable chatbot.enable_shell in configuration when needed

title: Compare teams using stronger evidence
summary: Expanded benchmark comparisons track repeated runs, cost and completion outcomes. Delivery and review policy now make missing test evidence and incomplete delivery clearer.
benefit: Choose team settings based on measured results and understand why a run was held.
where: Benchmarks and run reports

title: See chat tools working live
summary: Chat can list repository files and show tool calls while an answer is being prepared. Each conversation keeps its own history.
benefit: See what the assistant is checking instead of waiting on an unexplained pause.
where: Chat

title: Follow one task across its retries
summary: Work groups retries under a single task by default. Turn on Every attempt to inspect the earlier runs. Held PRs can get immediate fix-up runs.
benefit: The task list is easier to follow when the swarm repairs its own work.
where: Work → Every attempt

title: Catch unexpected visual changes
summary: Golden screenshot comparisons can block publication when a visual regression exceeds the configured threshold. CLI commands manage baseline screenshots and comparisons.
benefit: UI changes are checked against an established appearance, alongside code tests.
where: Run review evidence; CLI: swarmforge visual regress / update-golden

title: Clearer delivery failures
summary: Local branch delivery retries its push and reports when delivery did not succeed.
benefit: A finished run no longer hides a failed attempt to deliver its code.
where: Work → run report

title: Check layouts at phone, tablet and desktop widths
summary: A responsive-layout check screenshots a dashboard tab at 375, 768 and 1280 pixel viewports and inspects the DOM for overflowing or clipped elements. Problems are reported as findings that feed the same repair pipeline as other review findings.
benefit: Layout breakage on phones or tablets is caught automatically instead of surfacing during manual inspection.
where: CLI: swarmforge visual check-layout
